title: Rivet: the holy memory of great servants, praise without flattery, and nothing that requires them to hear
source_text: XXXIX. De hominibus vero loquens, Si qui fuerint, inquit, qui claruerint magnis virtutibus, maxime pietate in Deum, & meritis erga Ecclesiam, eorum memoria nobis sancta est & veneranda; de iis reverenter loquimur, eorum virtutes recolimus, nobis & aliis ad imitandum proponimus, eos prosequimur debitis laudibus. Et si quid aliud sit quod iis quos non videmus, & qui non audiunt nos, deferre possimus: quod genus honoris & cultus eo magis est aestimandum, quod ab omni adulatione alienum est, nec potest proficisci nisi ab ea mente, quae de eorum excellentia persuasa est, & eorum dignitatem magni facit, citra ullum propriae utilitatis respectum.
pass_a_gloss: Speaking of men, he says: If there have been any who have been illustrious for great virtues, especially piety toward God and merits toward the Church, their memory is holy and venerable to us; we speak of them reverently, we recollect their virtues, we set them before ourselves and others to be imitated, we attend them with due praises. And if there is anything else which we can pay to those whom we do not see, and who do not hear us: which kind of honor and cult is the more to be esteemed, because it is alien from all flattery, and cannot proceed except from a mind persuaded of their excellence, which makes much of their dignity, without any regard to its own advantage.
pass_b_english: People illustrious for virtue, above all for piety toward God and service of the Church, have a holy and venerable memory.
They are spoken of reverently, their virtues are recalled, they are proposed for imitation, and they receive due praise.
Any further honor must be such as can be paid to people we do not see and who do not hear us.
That kind is worth more because it cannot be flattery or self-interest.

lemmas.gloss: without any regard to one's own advantage

choices.why: The limit excludes any honor that needs the dead to hear the speaker.
rejected: who are present in their images
